activities.label: product_rule_model
activities.title: Product rule as two parts
activities.body: Read the model and note the two factor derivatives. Then move to the recall prompt.

essentialIdeas: Product rule differentiates a product by adding the derivative of the first factor times the second factor and the first factor times the derivative of the second factor.

activities.label: product_rule_explain
activities.title: Explain the product rule
activities.body: In your own words, explain how to differentiate a product of two functions. Keep it brief and specific.
activities.concept: Product rule
activities.correctAnswer: Differentiate each factor one at a time and add the two results: first derivative times second factor plus first factor times second derivative.
activities.feedback: A complete answer names both terms and shows that both factors stay in the expression. If you only describe multiplying derivatives, repair that to the two-term sum.

activities.label: product_rule_repair
activities.title: Fix the product rule step
activities.body: Correct the rule using the feedback and try again in one sentence.
activities.concept: Product rule
activities.correctAnswer: The derivative of a product is the derivative of the first factor times the second factor plus the first factor times the derivative of the second factor.
activities.feedback: This keeps both original factors and adds the two terms. That is the structure to use on any product of functions.

activities.label: chain_rule_model
activities.title: Chain rule for composites
activities.body: Read the model and notice the outer part and inner part. Then move to the recall prompt.

essentialIdeas: Chain rule differentiates a composite function by taking the outer derivative at the inner function and multiplying by the inner derivative.

activities.label: chain_rule_check
activities.title: Which rule fits here?
activities.body: Choose the correct derivative rule for a composite function. Then answer from memory if needed.
activities.concept: Chain rule
choices: Differentiate the outer function at the inner function, then multiply by the inner derivative.
Differentiate each part separately and add them.
Multiply the derivatives of the inside and outside functions without substitution.
Differentiate only the inside function and leave the outside unchanged.
activities.correctAnswer: Differentiate the outer function at the inner function, then multiply by the inner derivative.
activities.feedback: A composite function uses the outer derivative evaluated at the inner expression, then multiplies by the derivative of the inner part. The other choices miss either substitution or the multiplying step.

activities.title: Pause and return later
activities.body: Write one thing to review again later. Then end the session.
